title: Cohort onboarding playbook for private tenancies + failure budgeting
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a repeatable, quarter-aligned onboarding playbook for cohorts of private (VPC / on-prem) customers that ties to OKRs, defines failure budgets per cohort, and provides step-by-step runbooks for engineering, SRE, solutions, and CS. This ticket scopes the PM deliverable: playbook content, acceptance criteria, milestone schedule, and stakeholder sign-offs.

Why this work: As more customers adopt isolated deployments we need an operationalized path that balances safety (SLOs, auditability) with speed of activation. A documented cohort playbook reduces support overhead, standardizes rollout decisioning, and enables predictable capacity planning + cost hedging.

Scope included:
- Cohort definitions and gating criteria (pilot, early-access, general availability).
- Failure budgeting model per cohort (SLO vs activation pace) and how to map to rollout windows.
- Pre-activation checklist (security scans, KMS/HSM verification, network tests, IP allowlists).
- Activation runbook steps for Solutions + SRE with escalation matrix.
- Rollback criteria and automated rollback triggers (for compatibility or regressions).
- OKR mapping: links from this playbook to product OKRs and operational health metrics.
- Handoff templates for CS: cutover checklist, customer comms, SLA expectations.

Out of scope: detailed infra implementation work (ENG tickets will be separate), commercial contracting, and bespoke integrations for individual tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook draft published in Confluence with clear sections for pilot/EarlyAccess/GA

decisions: Trade-off: prioritize conservative failure budgets for Q2 pilots to reduce customer risk at the expense of activation velocity.
Decision: use cohort-based capacity hedging (pilot=2x buffer, early-access=1.3x, GA=1.0x) rather than per-tenant fixed buffers to simplify capacity ops.
Decision: require security attestation step for any tenant requesting FIPS/HSM — this will be a hard gate for GA enrollment.
Trade-off: defer automated rollback integration with routing policies until after two successful pilots to limit scope for Q2.
Routing policy note: prefer region-aware warm-up; avoid multi-region simultaneous activations for pilot cohorts.
